top_quotes.text: $NVDA Nvidia stock is experiencing downward pressure primarily due to broader tech sector rotation, lingering macroeconomic interest rate concerns, and investors digesting news from the Computex conference regarding increased industry competition.Key factors driving the stock's movement include:Sector Rotation & Profit-Taking: Following massive, historic rallies, many investors are locking in gains and rotating capital into lagging stocks.Rising Industry Competition: At the Computex technology conference in Taiwan, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced new chip lineups, but investors are simultaneously weighing growing competitive pushes from peers like Google, Amazon, and AMD, who are advancing their own in-house AI chips.Macroeconomic Pressures: Broader semiconductor and tech stocks are seeing volatility as investors monitor rising geopolitical tensions and anticipate the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decisions.

$IREN  comes down to one number: $70. 
 
That is NVIDIA's strike. Their 5yr $3.4B AI cloud deal gave $NVDA the right to buy 30M shares at $70, a $2.1B strategic stake, with up to 5GW of NVIDIA-aligned buildout ahead. 
 
So $70 is not a random chart line, it is the level NVIDIA is anchored to. IREN has since stacked the capital to build it: a $3.65B GPU financing and a $4.4B ARR Blackwell target. 
 
Right now it is coiled just under $70. A clean break and hold above $70 is where the NVIDIA economics turn on.  
 
$70 is the line.

data_quality.directive: Each flag marks a figure that failed an automated coherence check. Do NOT present a flagged comparable's affected ratio as fact: exclude it from any peer median or 'cheap/expensive vs peers' argument, and either omit it or footnote it as suspect with the stated reason. 'currency_mismatch' — the issuer reports in a currency other than its trading currency (e.g. an ADR); the yfinance ratio is not certifiable, so source that comp's multiples externally per the peer-comp rigor rule. 'peer_outlier'/'implausible' — verify against the primary filing before citing; it may be real-but-extreme or a data artifact.
